description: Implementation of the Suraksha Student Insurance Programme for the year 2026/27
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-10-19 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- The Suraksha Student Insurance Programme has been launched with the primary objective of creating an environment that enables students whose education is disrupted due to various health issues to overcome these obstacles and continue their studies without interruption. Students studying in government schools, government-approved private schools, Pirivenas, and assisted special schools are eligible to receive benefits under the said programme. The Hon. Prime Minister, in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education, informed the Cabinet that steps will be taken to amend and implement the existing Agreement between the Ministry of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education and Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation General Limited pertaining to the implementation of the said Student Insurance Programme, including the following new benefits as well, covering the period from 2026-09-01 to 2027-08-31, and the Cabinet decided to grant its concurrence for the same:

Providing the opportunity to obtain benefits up to Rs.75,000/- for the repair of hearing accessories and related service charges.


Providing the opportunity to obtain benefits up to Rs.20,000/- for students receiving long-term medication for Chronic Kidney Disease and Chronic Inflammatory Arthritis.


Providing the opportunity to obtain benefits up to Rs.20,000/- to cover the costs incurred for Malignancy Screening Test for Skin Cancer and Post-transplant Lymphoproliferative Disorder (PLTD), Screening Test for Osteoporosis and Screening Test for Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C and HIV Test.


Amending the term 'Cancer Treatment' listed under the Critical Illness category as 'Cancer Treatment and related Testing', and covering expenses for major surgeries for hip, shoulder, and knee joint replacement due to accidents as well as PET scans under the critical illness category.


Providing the opportunity to obtain benefits up Rs.100,000/- under the category of accidents in the event of student deaths resulting from accidents within or outside the school premises during activities (educational field trips and sports events etc.) that are organized by institutions under the purview of the Ministries of Education, Higher Education, or Vocational Education, and conducted under the supervision of educational authorities.
